_readme: Per-run monitoring log, one file per calendar day (America/Phoenix), used to generate the Daily PDF Report. Distinct from cases.json, which is the permanent case/review-queue index.
_run_note: Fifth scheduled Mon-Fri run. Product-count deltas since 2026-09-17: Hillside Rose Farm 146->145, Rose Explosion 1416->1418, Your Roses 1656->0. None of the newly listed products matched an active (Registered or Pending) trademark name, and no previously recorded listing disappeared from a reachable site. 120 of the 156 existing cases were re-verified present in their site's current catalog feed. The remaining 36 could not be checked because their sites were unreachable: 3 at Flower Meadow Dream (our egress proxy, unchanged) and 33 at Your Roses, which began returning a security-firewall 403 from its own server sometime after yesterday's run. Redland Ranch Roses returned 0 matches this run against 2 yesterday: the two were a peony and a heuchera, and the non-rose filter added 2026-09-17 now discards them before matching, which is the intended behaviour rather than a change at the site. WIDENED SCOPE THIS RUN: per user instruction 2026-09-18 the crawl now matches product titles against every name in the Master Trademark Filing Chart (271 names) rather than the 93 Registered and Pending ones only. The other 182 chart records had never been compared against a product title at all. That first widened pass created 124 cases, none of them Registered or Pending: 56 against chart entries with no status, 31 To Be Filed, 18 Abandoned, 18 Not Applicable, 1 Do Not File. 68 are classified Possible -- a single common word matching inside a longer title -- and each carries its chart status so it cannot be read as an enforceable finding.

sites.notes: Facebook page; facebook.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage, so the page was never reached. No open product feed exists for a Facebook page in any case.
Etsy storefront; etsy.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage. The seller's own site (ergongzy.com) was crawled in full and carries the same catalog.

Not reached. Both www.myroseworld.com and myroseworld.com were refused by this environment's egress proxy at the CONNECT stage, so the request never reached the seller's server. This is our own network policy, not a block by the site. Unchanged since 2026-09-16. The site's 3 existing cases (MYROSEWORL-001..003) could not be re-verified today and keep their 2026-09-16 Last Verified date.
Etsy shop closed (dormant). Roster entry retained per user instruction (2026-09-15); expected to stay inaccessible and not awaiting any decision.

Reached on the apex host after the www host was refused by the egress proxy. The Shopify feed returned HTTP 200 with an empty product array -- the store genuinely lists no products. Counted as checked, zero products.
Etsy storefront; etsy.com is blocked by this environment's network egress policy at the CONNECT stage.

NEW THIS RUN -- and a different kind of block from the others. The CONNECT succeeded (our proxy returned '200 Connection Established'), then the seller's own server answered HTTP 403 with 'Your request was blocked by the security firewall' -- a LiteSpeed/Hostinger WAF response, not our network policy. Every catalog path was refused this way (/wp-json/wp/v2/product, /products.json, the site root); only /sitemap.xml answered, and it redirected. The site served 1,656 products through its WordPress feed as recently as 2026-09-17, so this is a change at the seller's end within the last day. No attempt was made to work around the firewall, per the standing rule against bypassing website security controls. The site's 33 existing cases (YOURROSES-001..033) could not be re-verified today and keep their 2026-09-17 Last Verified date. If this persists, it needs a decision on how to verify that catalog.

screenshot_limitation: Still no case has a screenshot on file -- same network-proxy limitation as prior runs (headless Chromium cannot complete a connection through this environment's egress proxy). Explained to the user in chat on 2026-09-14; awaiting their choice of approach (manual capture vs. Wayback Machine vs. environment-level fix).
